one_line: A five-minute walkthrough of making songs in Suno AI (custom lyrics, style, vocal or instrumental tracks) plus its free-tier limits; a basic consumer tutorial with no engineering content.
summary: The host walks through Suno AI, a web tool that generates full music tracks from text. The workflow is: log in, open the Create tab, turn on Custom Mode, supply lyrics (either written in ChatGPT and pasted in, or generated by Suno from a topic), enter a style description, and click Create. Each generation returns two track variants, and the host prefers the second one. For instrumental tracks, the host turns on the instrumental toggle, enters a style and title, and generates again. The host recommends Suno's style and genre list to steer output. The video closes with the free-tier allowance (50 credits per day, about 10 songs) and a pointer to paid plans, plus a promotional aside about Suno. Nothing in the video touches models, evals, or engineering practice, and the claims about quality are the host's own impressions. The video is dated 2024-11-02, so the pricing it cites may be out of date.

key_ideas.idea: Custom Mode in the Create tab is the path that exposes lyrics, style and title controls.
key_ideas.detail: The host enables Custom Mode before entering any input. That is the only setup step shown beyond logging in.

key_ideas.idea: Lyrics can come from either ChatGPT or Suno itself.
key_ideas.detail: Option one is to ask ChatGPT for lyrics and paste them in. Option two is to type a topic into Suno and let it write the lyrics. The host claims Suno's lyrics are better than ChatGPT's, but no side-by-side comparison is shown.

key_ideas.idea: One Create click returns two track variants.
key_ideas.detail: The host says Suno gave two options and that both came from a single click. Listening to them is the only evaluation method shown; the host plays one, then the other, and prefers the second.

key_ideas.idea: Instrumental output is a toggle, not a separate tool.
key_ideas.detail: The host turns on the instrumental option, adds a style, writes a title and clicks Create. The same generation flow applies.

key_ideas.idea: The style and genre list is the main lever for steering output.
key_ideas.detail: The host recommends the list Suno provides so the user can request a specific sound. The host's example was a result that felt like a movie chase-scene soundtrack.

techniques.name: Suno custom-mode song generation
techniques.how: 1) Log in with any offered sign-in option. 2) Open the Create tab and turn on Custom Mode. 3) Get lyrics either from ChatGPT (paste them in) or by typing a topic so Suno writes them. 4) Enter the music style. Suno pre-fills a title, which can be kept or changed. 5) Click Create and pick the better of the two returned variants.
techniques.when: Making a full song with lyrics for casual or hobby use, with no setup beyond the web UI.

techniques.name: Instrumental track generation
techniques.how: In Custom Mode, turn on the instrumental toggle, enter a style, enter a title, and click Create. Lyrics are not needed.
techniques.when: Background music, soundtracks or beats where vocals are not wanted.

techniques.name: Steering with the style and genre list
techniques.how: Open Suno's style and genre list and pick the genre or descriptors that match the target sound before writing the style field.
techniques.when: The first generation does not sound like what you wanted and you need a more specific style description.

tools: Suno AI (web app, Create tab, Custom Mode, instrumental toggle)

numbers.claim: Each Create action returns two track variants.
Free tier: 50 credits per day, which the host says allows up to 10 songs per day.
Paid plans exist for users who need more songs, with no prices given in the video.

hot_takes: The claim that Suno's lyrics beat ChatGPT's is an unsupported opinion. No comparison is shown.
Quality judgments rest only on the host's listening impressions, with no criteria given.
The free-tier numbers are dated (video from 2024-11-02, read in 2026). Verify current limits on Suno's site before relying on them.

Scored quality 2 because the content is a thin consumer walkthrough with a promotional aside and a link call-to-action, and it has no sponsorship disclosure. It has no relevance to AgentOS, the gateway or ProsHarness.

relevance.why: A consumer music-generation UI. Nothing here touches the proxy, memory, inference, or evals.
No Claude Code, checkpointing, approvals or skill content.
